title: Boolean Conversion, Truthy and Falsy Values

content.explanation: Computers ultimately make decisions using only two states: true and false. Because of this, JavaScript can convert any value into a Boolean. This process is called Boolean conversion. JavaScript has a small set of falsy values that automatically convert to false. These include false, 0, -0, 0n, an empty string (""), null, undefined, and NaN. Every other value is considered truthy and converts to true. This behavior is heavily used in conditions, loops, validation logic, and short-circuit operators. Understanding truthy and falsy values is important because many JavaScript bugs occur when developers incorrectly assume how a value behaves in a condition. One of the most common interview traps is that empty arrays ([]) and empty objects ({}) are truthy because they are objects, not because they contain data. Professional developers rely on explicit checks when business rules require precise validation.
content.example: Boolean([]) returns true and Boolean({}) returns true, even though both appear empty.
content.analogy: Falsy values are like a very short guest list. Everyone not on the list automatically gets allowed into the event.
content.keyTakeaway: Only a few values are falsy; almost everything else in JavaScript is truthy.

revisionSummary: Learn the falsy list; everything else is truthy.

mcqs.question: What is a falsy value?
options: A value that becomes false during Boolean conversion
A value that cannot be stored
A value that is always undefined
A value that causes an error
mcqs.explanation: Falsy values convert to false when evaluated as booleans.

mcqs.question: Why are truthy and falsy values important?
options: They determine how values behave in conditions
mcqs.explanation: JavaScript uses truthiness when evaluating conditions and logical expressions.

mcqs.question: What is the result of Boolean('hello')?
mcqs.explanation: A non-empty string is a truthy value.

mcqs.question: A developer writes if([]) { console.log('Run'); }. What happens?
mcqs.explanation: Arrays are objects, and all objects are truthy.

mcqs.question: An empty array ([]) is a falsy value.
mcqs.explanation: Arrays are objects, and objects are truthy even when empty.
